subject: Girls on the Run Program and 5K
overview: Host Danielle Balocca interviewed coach Aoife Mary and several participants about the Girls on the Run program's mission and its upcoming celebratory 5k event. The discussion detailed the program's history, its social-emotional curriculum, and various ways for the Medford community to get involved.

items.title: Introduction and Local Favorites
items.summary: Danielle Balocca introduced guest Aoife Mary, a coach who recommended Donuts with a Difference as a local community staple.

items.title: Program History and Mission
items.summary: Mary described the program's origins in North Carolina and its growth into a national organization serving over two million girls.

items.title: Curriculum and Program Structure
items.summary: The program combines bi-weekly running practices with a specific curriculum focused on social-emotional growth and positive behaviors.

items.title: Accessibility and Financial Assistance
items.summary: Organizers highlighted that the program is open to all physical abilities and provides financial aid to ensure affordability for all families.

items.title: Coaching Motivations and Community Impact
items.summary: Mary discussed her background in the fitness industry and her desire to help girls develop healthy relationships with exercise and body image at a young age.

items.title: Community Involvement and Volunteering
items.summary: The discussion outlined various ways for residents to participate, including coaching, sponsoring participants, or serving as running buddies.

items.title: Fall Season Celebratory 5K
items.summary: The season concludes with a non-competitive 5k event at Hormel Stadium on November 20th involving approximately 800 girls from the Greater Boston area.

items.title: The Five C's Curriculum
items.summary: Mary detailed the five core values of the curriculum: competence, confidence, connection, character, and caring.

items.title: Participant Interviews
items.summary: Program participants Kay, Audrey, and Parker shared their personal accomplishments and advice for new runners in the program.
